title: Scope is a pre-flight guard, not a seventh check
context: Phase B introduced per-user scope (which legal entities of the corporate group a user may act for). Phase B.2 needed to enforce that on writes. The obvious option — adding SCOPE as a seventh CheckOutcome inside CheckEngine — would break the well-known 'six checks' product concept everywhere it's referenced (docs, deck, panel copy, tests).
decision: Scope is a PRE-FLIGHT guard: `scope_service.require_scope(session, caller, entity_id)` runs BEFORE the six-check gate on every write endpoint. If the user has no scope for the entity, the request is refused with 403 ROLE_NOT_HELD and the CheckEngine is never invoked. This preserves the six-check semantics and matches the enterprise-treasury pattern that separates 'is this person authorised' from 'does this deal meet policy'.

shape.guard_signature: require_scope(session, caller, entity_id) -> None (raises TreasuryError on refusal)
shape.error_message_shape: You do not have scope for NG_DE. Ask an administrator to grant you access.

schema_changes.backfill_strategy: Seed backfills existing rows via LEGAL_ENTITY_BY_CURRENCY: GBP -> NG_UK, EUR -> NG_DE, USD -> NG_US, CHF -> NG_UK. Real production migrations would need a client-specific mapping table.

frontend_surface.auth_me: GET /auth/me now returns scope.entities — the entities the caller may act for. This is the source the ticket + hedge modal read to render the entity picker.
frontend_surface.hedge_modal: New 'Book under legal entity' dropdown. Defaults to the currency-matching scoped entity, else the first scoped one. Only shown if the user has any scope.

still_todo: Thread legal_entity_id through the deposit Ticket (frontend) — currently the backend accepts it but the ticket UI doesn't send one; POST defaults to null and no scope guard fires. That's Phase B.3.
Thread scope through the PlannerService allocations so a user with UK-only scope only sees UK-eligible names.
Tag HedgeLink with legal_entity_id (currently derived from the linked exposure).
invariants: The six-check gate stays 'six checks'. Scope is a separate preflight.
A write endpoint that accepts legal_entity_id must call require_scope before its business logic.
The audit_event log records both the scope grant/revoke history (Phase B) and the failed-scope refusals (via ErrorCode logs).
